group.title: Around town
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A shop that makes and sells bread and cakes.
examples: I buy fresh bread at the {bakery}.
wrong: We wash our clothes at the bakery.

words.meaning: A small place where you can buy coffee and simple food.
examples: Let’s meet at the {cafe} for coffee.
wrong: I sleep at the cafe every night with my family.

words.meaning: A building where you go to watch films on a big screen.
examples: We saw a funny film at the {movie theater}.
wrong: I cook dinner in the movie theater at home.

words.meaning: A building where Christians go to pray.
examples: The old {church} has a tall tower.
wrong: The church is a small animal that lives in trees.

words.meaning: A thing with walls and a roof, like a house or an office.
examples: My office is in that tall {building}.
wrong: The building flew over the trees like a bird.

words.meaning: A shop that sells books.
examples: I bought a new novel at the {bookstore}.
wrong: You can buy fresh fish at the bookstore.

words.meaning: A thing in a park or square that sends water up into the air.
examples: Children play near the {fountain} in the park.
wrong: The fountain was dry because it sends out sand.

words.meaning: A long seat for two or more people, often outside.
examples: We sat on a {bench} in the park.
wrong: I put the bench in my pocket.

words.meaning: An outside place with swings and slides for children.
examples: The kids are on the slide at the {playground}.
wrong: The playground is a place where children cannot play.

words.meaning: A tall, narrow building or part of a building.
examples: You can see the whole city from the {tower}.
wrong: The tower is very short and wide.

words.meaning: A place where people live that is bigger than a village but smaller than a city.
examples: I grew up in a small {town}.
wrong: Our town is so small that only one fish lives there.

words.meaning: The middle part of a town or city, with many shops.
examples: The bank is in the town {center}.
wrong: The center is at the far edge of the town.

words.meaning: A building where firefighters and their trucks wait.
examples: The red trucks leave the {fire station} fast.
wrong: We buy bread and milk at the fire station.

words.meaning: The building where the people who run a town work.
examples: The mayor works at the {town hall}.
wrong: The town hall is a long room in my apartment.

words.meaning: A place where you go to get your hair cut.
examples: She got a short haircut at the {hair salon}.
wrong: I went to the hair salon to buy apples.

words.meaning: A big building with many shops inside.
examples: We went shopping at the {mall} on Saturday.
wrong: The mall has no shops at all.

words.meaning: A machine in the street where you get cash from your bank.
examples: I need cash, so I’ll stop at the {ATM}.
wrong: I took a hot pizza out of the ATM.

words.meaning: The door or place where you go into a building.
examples: Meet me at the main {entrance}.
wrong: We left the building through the entrance on the way out.

words.meaning: The door or place where you go out of a building.
examples: The {exit} is at the back of the store.
wrong: We came into the room through the exit sign on the window.

words.meaning: A board with words or pictures that tells you something.
examples: The {sign} says the shop is closed.
wrong: The sign was empty, so it told us the way.

words.meaning: A room with a toilet in a public place.
examples: Excuse me, where is the {restroom}?
wrong: I made a cake in the restroom of the restaurant.

words.meaning: A shop that sells shoes and boots.
examples: I got new sneakers at the {shoe store}.
wrong: I bought eggs and milk at the shoe store.

words.meaning: A shop that sells things for children to play with.
examples: He bought a ball at the {toy store}.
wrong: The toy store only sells cars for adults to drive.

words.meaning: A shop that sells food and things for the home.
examples: We need milk from the {grocery store}.
wrong: I bought a new bed at the grocery store.

words.meaning: A shop that sells medicine and things for washing.
examples: I bought cough medicine at the {drugstore}.
wrong: The drugstore sells only cars.

words.meaning: A shop that sells animals and food for them.
examples: We got a fish at the {pet store}.
wrong: The pet store sells only cars and bikes.

words.meaning: A box where you put letters to send them.
examples: I put the letter in the {mailbox}.
wrong: I keep my milk cold in the mailbox.

words.meaning: A figure of a person or animal made of stone or metal.
examples: There is a {statue} of a horse in the square.
wrong: The statue walked to the shop and bought bread.

words.meaning: A door in a fence or wall, often outside.
examples: Please close the {gate} to the garden.
wrong: The gate is a hole in the sky.

words.meaning: A building with many floors where you leave your car.
examples: We left the car in the {parking garage}.
wrong: I swim every morning in the parking garage.

words.meaning: The most important street in a town, with many shops.
examples: There are lots of cafes on {Main Street}.
wrong: Main Street is the smallest, quietest road in town.

words.meaning: Very close, at the side of something.
examples: The bank is {next to} the bakery.
wrong: The cafe is next to the bank, far away in another city.

words.meaning: Just before something, facing it.
examples: The bus stops {in front of} the school.
wrong: I stood in front of the house, behind it in the garden.

words.meaning: A place where you can buy things.
examples: The {store} on the corner sells milk.
wrong: The store gives everything away and sells nothing.

words.meaning: A shop that sells flowers and plants.
examples: I bought roses at the {flower shop}.
wrong: I bought a sofa at the flower shop.

words.meaning: A shop that sells things to wear.
examples: She bought a dress at the {clothing store}.
wrong: I bought bread and cheese at the clothing store.

words.meaning: A place where men go to get their hair cut.
examples: Dad gets his hair cut at the {barber shop}.
wrong: I bought new shoes at the barber shop.

words.meaning: A place in a mall with many small places to eat.
examples: We had lunch at the {food court}.
wrong: There is no food at the food court.

words.meaning: A big building where people or machines make things.
examples: My uncle works in a car {factory}.
wrong: The factory is a quiet place where nothing is made.

words.meaning: A tall light at the side of a road.
examples: The {streetlights} come on at night.
wrong: The streetlight was so dark we could not see.
